blockLag.description: §3.15 (0.5.1): chain head minus the mirror's last-applied block (`liveBlockNumber`), from one eth_blockNumber taken at status time. Declared since 0.5.0 and never populated until now. ABSENT — together with headBlockNumber and headSampledAt — when the RPC read fails: never 0, never null (§3.14). A nonzero lag is the NORMAL resting state of a healthy mirror, because liveBlockNumber does not advance on a block that produced no world events; it is information, not a fault, and `meta.stale` is NOT derived from it.

checkpoint.description: §3.5: the last Kamigaze-consistent checkpoint, plus `inFlight` (0.6.3) — whether one is being written right now. NULL before the first LIVE, and then never again; a checkpoint cannot be in flight before the first has been adopted, so null hides no state. `inFlight` is answerable at all only because the write moved off the main thread (DESIGN §3.5, divergence 16): before 0.6.3 a `status` asked during a checkpoint did not return for 20-32 s. additionalProperties stays true — the report's own fields are the daemon's CheckpointReport and are not re-declared here.

inFlight.description: a checkpoint refresh is running in the checkpoint child right now. Additive in 0.6.3 (ADDITIVE_LEAVES_063).

feedsDegraded.description: §1.2 (0.5.2): Kamiden FEED health, shaped like `degraded` so a caller gates on it the same way, and kept separate from it because `degraded` is chain-only and drives meta.stale (§3.2). 'kamiden-stream:<state>' whenever the stream is not live; 'kamiden-silent:<N>s' past SILENT_STALL_MS. Empty array when healthy — never absent.

enrich.description: §3.12 payload enrichment. Always present, so the switch is visible whether it is on or off — the one key by which a flag-off 0.4.0 answer differs from 0.3.0 (G3.g).

reconcileIntervalMs.description: §3.17 (0.6.0): period of the sync layer's periodic chain reconcile. 0 = disabled, and status.sync carries the same number so a reader can tell a backstop that is off from one that has simply not fired.

stateCdnUrl.description: §3.1 (0.6.2): the S3/CloudFront state export a cold boot streams its full image from. ABSENT when switched off, like every other optional URL here — and then a cold boot takes the Kamigaze gRPC path byte for byte. Unlike the others its baked default is SET (the production value the deployed web client ships), so absence here means someone turned it off; `configSources.stateCdnUrl` says at which level.

rpcReads.description: §3.13 (0.5.0): health of the ONE chain read the query layer makes (the account gas balance). Reported here for exactly the reason the per-feed Kamiden block is: the answer that needed it simply OMITS the block, so a reader must be able to tell "this account holds nothing" from "the read did not happen".

lastError.description: Present only when a read has failed: an omitted key means none has.

headBlockNumber.description: §3.15 (0.5.1): the chain head this lag was computed against. Served beside the lag so the subtraction is auditable rather than asserted.

headSampledAt.description: §3.15 (0.5.1): when the head read landed (§3.8 clock). A head number of unknown age is not evidence.

Sync.description: §3.17 (0.6.0): health of the sync layer's own recovery, all counters since PROCESS START (a restart zeroes them). Deliberately not tripwires: `reconnects` is nonzero within a minute of every healthy start, because the production stream server closes the subscription every ~30-40 s by design, and a tripwire marks the daemon degraded. The one condition here that IS a chain-correctness fault reaches `degraded` as `unhealed-ranges:<N>`.

reconnects.description: raw stream (re)subscriptions after the first. Its healthy resting state RISES: the server closes the subscription roughly every 30-40 s by design.

gapsHealed.description: recovery ranges read from the chain and applied.

gapsDeferred.description: recovery ranges NOT applied — the RPC node was behind the range end, or the subscription was torn down mid-heal. Each one is recorded in unhealedRanges; nothing was partially applied.

reconcilePasses.description: periodic reconcile ticks processed, including the ones whose range was empty (the common case).

reconciledThrough.description: every block up to and including this one has been covered by a COMPLETE chain range read. Unlike `liveBlockNumber` — which is the block of the last APPLIED EVENT and so does not move across event-less blocks (§3.15) — this advances whether or not the range carried logs, which makes it the honest lower bound on what the mirror has actually read. null until the bootstrap gap-fill seeds it.

lastReconcileAt.description: when the last reconcile tick was processed (ISO). null before the first one.

unhealedRanges.description: block ranges [from, to] that recovery could not apply, oldest first, capped at 64. NON-EMPTY MEANS THE MIRROR IS KNOWN-INCOMPLETE over those blocks. The periodic reconcile retries them; a list that survives two reconcile intervals raises `unhealed-ranges:<N>` in `degraded`.

lastHealMs.description: wall duration of the most recent heal attempt, successful or deferred.

reconcileIntervalMs.description: the configured reconcile period, echoed here so a reader can tell a backstop that is switched off (0) from one that has simply not fired yet.

LastFullLoad.description: §3.1 (0.6.2): which source served this PROCESS's full state load, and how long it took. NULL on a warm boot, which resumed a cached image and ran no full load — that is the normal restart and not a fault; a load that FAILED never reaches LIVE at all, so null never means "it went wrong". The same fact is logged as `[state] full load served by CDN|gRPC`; this field exists so a reader does not have to hold the log.

source.description: 'cdn' = the S3/CloudFront state export; 'grpc' = the Kamigaze snapshot service. A configured CDN that DECLINED (unreadable manifest, nonce disagreement, warm-enough cache) or that failed mid-load reads 'grpc' here — the fallback is the contract, and `config.stateCdnUrl` says whether it was configured at all.

prefix.description: the export's own key prefix, e.g. '96/33437307/2026-09-18T02Z'. Present only on the CDN path. It is what identifies WHICH image was loaded: nonce and block do not identify one on their own, and the exporter owns the layout.

block.description: the Kamigaze block the loaded image is stamped at (cache.lastKamigazeBlock). The gap from here to the stream's start is what the bridge closes.

nonce.description: the Kamigaze nonce of the loaded image. A change against a previously synced nonce is counted in tripwires.kamigazeNonceBumps.

seconds.description: wall seconds the load took, CDN or gRPC. The number the two paths are compared by.
